newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's LUKoil plans higher investment in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia's LUKoil plans higher investment in 1997.

text.p: LUKoil, Russia's largest oil company, plans capital investment this year of 9.0-10.5 trillion roubles, up 20 percent from 1996, President Vagit Alekperov told an annual shareholders meeting Thursday.
He did not detail where the money would be invested, but his written address in the 1996 annual report said the company made the bulk of its investments last year in oil production.
"The overall amount of investment in production in 1996 was over six trillion roubles," Alekperov wrote. "In 1997, we plan to increase investments by over 20 percent."

The written address also said investments in overseas projects rose last year. "Investment abroad rose -- in countries with highly productive (oil) reserves and low oil production and transport costs," he said.
LUKoil produced 58.5 million tonnes of oil (1.17 million barrels per day) in 1996, up two percent from 57.3 million (1.15 million bpd) in 1995.
It expects to increase output by two percent to 59.7 million tonnes (1.19 million bpd).
LUKoil produced 300,000 tonnes (6,000 bpd) outside Russia last year, up from 60,000 tonnes (1,200 bpd) in 1995.
It has launched an aggressive campaign to look outside Russia for new reserves, with major production deals already signed in the Caspian region and in Iraq.
